findings.reason: the cited census records "open plans with no section declarations at all; those are legacy plans outside this plan's scope", yet the rule as written classifies every one of them closable and pulls them out of `ready_now` and the ready counts, so the node would change readiness for a population §1 excludes and §2's section-bearing fixtures cannot catch it.
findings.text: §2 defines closable as "no implementable section, so every section is done, descoped or deferred", but a plan with no section declarations at all also has no implementable section, and §1's own evidence names that population and puts it out of scope

findings.reason: on the verified data §3's mechanism leaves signal-search-finds-the-measured-signal and cut-cell-current-attribution blocked, so §6's done-when ("no plan reading `blocked` on a gate over finished work") is reached only through §4's descope path, an ordering §3 never states and its done-when never exercises; a §3 node reading "done or descoped" can implement the rule literally and leave two of §1's three examples still blocked.
findings.text: §3 clears an unpassed gate only when its gated sections are "all done or descoped", leaving `deferred` outside the rule, while §1 attributes two of the three blocked plans to gates whose gated section is deferred (imas-codex `g-ssfms-1` on `s11`; nova's three `g-cca-*` gates on `s6`)

findings.reason: with no caller named, a §5 node wires `closable: true` to an event that never fires, or silently invents a declaration write inside promotion; the plan must name the write path that ticks the declaration, or state that `crew complete`/`crew land` must itself gain it.
findings.text: §5 fires "[w]hen `crew complete` or `crew land` moves a plan's last implementable section to done", but neither command writes `section_declarations`: `reckon/crew/merge.py` writes no plan state at all, and the only landing-derived plan record is a run comment that `_landed_sections` (reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:1457) describes as recording "run outcomes, not document-card shape or section closure"

findings.reason: both branches are additive supersets of today's behaviour and neither §2's nor §3's done-when fixture depends on a descoped section existing, so the landing order is a scheduling nicety rather than something the mechanism needs.
findings.text: §2 and §3 both branch on the `descoped` declaration, which does not exist in the codebase (`grep -rn descoped reckon/` returns nothing; `_schema.SECTION_DECLARATION_ENUM` is `["implementable","deferred","done"]`) and is added only by `a-project-reads-as-one-picture` §9, yet only §4 declares that depends-on

response_events.reason: the descoped branches in §2 and §3 are additive: both rules read done and deferred today, treat descoped as done once a-project-reads-as-one-picture §9 lands, and neither fixture needs a descoped section; an edge would hold §2 and §3 behind §9 for no mechanism they require

wiring-1.reason: the descoped branches in §2 and §3 are additive: both rules read done and deferred today, treat descoped as done once a-project-reads-as-one-picture §9 lands, and neither fixture needs a descoped section; an edge would hold §2 and §3 behind §9 for no mechanism they require

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every citation resolves: the evidence archive exists and its figures match §1 exactly (1862/376/106 declarations; 21 plans at pct=100.0 split 3 blocked / 13 ready / 5 deferred; "15 of the 20" carry deferred sections — 5 of the 20 census rows list no deferred section); `a-project-reads-as-one-picture#s9` exists and is titled "A section can be descoped"; `a-sprint-closes-on-completable-work` exists with `plan-status=shipped`; `docs/evidence/derived-gate-state-landed.html` exists and lists `reckon/lifecycle.py`, which holds the named blocker function `unpassed_gate_blockers` (lifecycle.py:52); the `the-fleet-node-stays-in-service` gate `g-tfnsis-move-ready` carries `data-section="s5" data-gated-sections="s8"` exactly as §1 states; the nova `g-cca-...-admits-the-hot-path` gate is `closed` with `verdict="failed"` as §1 states; §4's "skill rule" resolves to `~/.claude/skills/reckon-build/references/coordinator-reference.md:984`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §2, §3, §4 each name an in-fixture control and a base-commit arm the test fails at; §5 names its control ("a landing that leaves an implementable section returns neither"); §6's control is the base census reporting the 21 plans of §1. Every done-when is measurable and falsifiable.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §1 cites `docs/evidence/archive/a-finished-plan-closes-landed.html`, an in-repo durable path that exists and carries the census; §6 writes before/after counts to the landed record. No scratchpad, node-local or session-temporary path appears anywhere in the plan.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the plan's new symbols are mechanism names (`closable`, `stale-gate`, `plan-closable`, `moved_to`); no plan label, stage name, ticket number, version tag or changelog prose reaches a symbol, comment or filename.
rubric_items.reasoning: findings — the stated root cause matches the cited evidence in §1, but §2's scope, §3's gate rule and §5's trigger each diverge from the code and evidence they rest on (FINDING lines below).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 (readiness gains `closable`), §3 (a gate on finished work stops holding), §4 (deferred work leaves before close), §5 (the finishing node offers its close), §6 (census closes or records). §3's `stale-gate` finding and §5's obligations row are the reporting surface of their one mechanism, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §2, §3 and §4 all build against the `descoped` declaration, but only §4 declares the depends-on edge (`plan-section-depends-on` s4 -> `a-project-reads-as-one-picture#s9`), while §2 (plan.html:67-68) and §3 (plan.html:88-90) name `descoped` in their own mechanism and declare nothing.
